unmapped_findings: Sample S5 (TA 1150 °C, TB 365 °C) achieved a product of strength and elongation (PSE) of 11,450 MPa·% (UTS 1315 MPa, El 8.7 %); the overall S5 PSE range across conditions was ≈10.7–11.5 GPa·%.

S5 steel exhibited the fastest bainitic transformation among the studied steels, with an incubation period completed within 10 s and complete bainitic transformation at 365 °C after 1000 s (and at 335 °C after 700 s).
The measured martensite-start temperature of S5 was 331 °C, the highest among the five steels; austempering at 365 °C (~34 °C above Ms) suppresses martensite and promotes bainitic transformation.
The addition of 0.78 wt.% Ni to S5 did not adversely affect the bainitic transformation kinetics and maintained the αp content at a minimal level via its austenite-stabilizing effect.

In S5, (Fe,M)xCy particles precipitate during cooling between approximately 700 °C and 1000 °C according to the TTP simulation; the resulting (Fe,M)xCy and MoC were less present in the final microstructure compared to steels S1–S3.

S5 was positioned, in terms of UTS–El performance, intermediate between steels containing ≈3 wt.% Al and ≈5 wt.% Al (literature alloys with 0.67–0.94 wt.% C): ≈3 wt.% Al alloys gave UTS 1400–2000 MPa and El 9–12 % (PSE ≈12,600–24,000 MPa·%), and ≈5 wt.% Al alloys gave UTS 1300–1850 MPa and El 4–9.5 % (PSE ≈5200–17,575 MPa·%).
MatCalc predicted a 100 K/s cooling-rate TTP diagram for S5 with T_B lines at 365 °C (Bt 1000 s) and 335 °C (Bt 700 s) - the shortest transformation times of the four simulated panels (Fig. 8 (d)).
